Month-end close from 10 days to 3
Reconciliations, journal entries, accruals, and intercompany matching, done before your team sits down with coffee. Exceptions get flagged with context, not a 200-row spreadsheet.
Reconciliations that match themselves
Bank, credit card, AR sub-ledger, intercompany: pulled, matched, and posted. Only true exceptions reach a human, with the source documents already attached.
AP and AR that runs without the inbox

Invoices captured from email and PDF, coded to the right GL account, routed for approval, and posted to the ERP. AR side: collections reminders, cash application, and aging reports go out on schedule.
AP without the data entry
Vendor invoices are read, validated against POs, coded, and queued for the right approver based on your delegation of authority.
Three-way match on PO, receipt, and invoice before posting.
Duplicate detection across vendors, amounts, and dates.
Audit log on every approval, with the original PDF attached.
AR that collects on time
Reminders go out before things age. Cash application matches deposits to invoices. Disputes get logged with context, not chased through email.
Auto-matched cash against open invoices, even with short pays.
Escalation rules by customer tier and DSO.
Aging dashboards updated live, not at month-end.
Loan origination and underwriting, without the manual checklist

The same document-capture-and-match approach we use for AP/AR applies to a loan file: application data, income docs, and KYC checklist items get pulled, verified against source documents, and assembled into a single underwriter-ready file. The credit decision itself always stays with a human underwriter, we do not automate approvals.
Application intake and KYC checklist

Application forms, pay stubs, bank statements, and ID documents are captured and checked against your KYC/AML checklist. Missing or inconsistent items are flagged before the file reaches underwriting.
Underwriter-ready summary

Traditional and alternative data (payment history, employment, bank transaction patterns) get assembled into one risk summary. The underwriter reviews and makes the call, with the source data attached.
Fraud and transaction monitoring that flags before it costs you

Transaction patterns, geolocation, and behavioral signals get scored continuously. Anomalies get diverted into a review queue with the supporting evidence attached, instead of clearing silently or blocking a legitimate customer.
Controls and audit trail your auditor will accept
Every automated action is logged with who triggered it, what changed, when, and against which approval rule. SOX-friendly by default. When PwC asks for evidence, you export a CSV.
Segregation of duties, preserved
Bots don't approve their own work. Approval rules and DoA matrices map to your existing controls. We don't ask you to relax them.
Evidence on demand
Sample selection, walkthroughs, and journal entry testing: pull the supporting documents from one place instead of three inboxes.
Reporting and FP&A without the copy-paste
Board packs, variance reports, and cash-flow forecasts pulled directly from the ERP. Numbers tie. Footnotes update. The CFO stops getting two different versions of the same KPI.
Variance analysis with the why
Material variances surface with the drivers attached (vendor, contract, GL line), not just a number in red.
Forecasts that roll forward
Actuals push into the model on close. No more rebuilding the rolling forecast every month.
